1.why: All eight screens are static single-card pages with no animations, banners, or pop-up elements visible.

2.why: Bold headings and high-contrast blue buttons with visible focus outlines stand out, but the large dark Logs panel gives equal visual weight to secondary content.

3.why: Each page presents one clearly labeled task so the needed input and button are quick to spot, though in step 2 the verification link and token sit below the card in the logs area and require some scanning.

4.why: The password rules are shown at the point of entry and the token and MFA code stay visible or pre-filled, so Helena must memorize little beyond her new password itself.

5.why: No screen offers a remember-me checkbox, autofill prompt, or password-manager support; only plain email, password, and code fields are present.

6.why: The entered email persists in step 2 and the recovery token appears pre-filled in step 3 exactly as displayed in the logs, letting the user recognize rather than recall values.

7.why: Card text uses short plain sentences such as 'Enter your account email address,' although the simulation info box and log lines contain technical phrasing like 'securely hashed.'

8.why: Only the success path is shown across the eight screenshots, so no error message is observable to confirm whether it would describe the problem and its fix.

9.why: No field provides a sample value or format example (the password screen states rules without illustrating one), though the exact token and MFA code values are displayed nearby for copying.

10.why: The flow offers a single fixed method (email link, token, new password, MFA code) and never presents alternative choices such as face login or code-only sign-in.

11.why: Every screen contains at most one input field and one primary button, never presenting multiple competing choices at once.

12.why: Each action is followed by explicit feedback, e.g. the green 'recovery instructions will be sent securely' message and log entries ending with 'Medication review appointment request confirmed.'

13.why: Short safety tips accompany each step, such as 'Never share this code,' 'Open links only from this hospital site,' and 'Do not share passwords or verification codes with anyone.'

14.why: The screenshots show only the happy path with no error or retry state, so ease of trying again after a mistake cannot be verified from what was observed.

15.why: All eight steps reuse the same header, card layout, button styling, logs panel, and footer, making the design predictable and learnable over time.
